about: Own-words reads from the daily research task (ADMIS, Rabobank, Czapp and the news feed). fund_score: -1 bearish to +1 bullish, a judgement on the fundamental news only.

cotton.fundamental: Dec is steadying at ~77.06 overnight, sitting right on Monday's broken 77.05 level with Mar ~81.06; nothing new on supply, and a still-firm dollar (DXY ~103.6) keeps the bounce shallow. For old-crop Dec/Mar the issue is whether funds keep liquidating into first notice; high-grade certs heading into Dec delivery remain a risk for longs, not a comfort.
events: Dec cotton ~77.06 early Tuesday, back at the 77.05 level after Monday's 76.95 settle; Mar ~81.06 (ICE via TradingView)
Dollar index holds near 103.6 after last week's jump (ICE via TradingView)

sugar.fundamental: Brazil still sets the tone: the real's slide on fiscal worries keeps Centre-South mills keen to hedge in local-currency terms, and Mar dipped to 17.97 overnight, briefly under 18.02 support, before steadying at ~18.07. Crude's rebound is a small help for the ethanol pull on cane, but not yet enough to change the mill-mix picture.
events: Mar sugar trades 17.97-18.22 early, ~18.07, testing 18.02 support (ICE via TradingView)
Brazilian real weakness on Lula fiscal concerns keeps hedge pressure on (Bloomberg)
Crude rebounds ~1.5% on Middle East shipping risk, a modest ethanol offset (Dow Jones)

coffee.fundamental: The exchange-stock squeeze is still driving nearby arabica: Dec is up ~3.85 at ~284.55 (high 288.30) as the market keeps pricing a shrinking ICE-certified pile, with Mar lagging at ~278.65, so the Dec/Mar inverse is widening. That spread says deliverable coffee, not Brazil's next crop, is the constraint; a weaker real remains the main brake on further gains.
events: Dec arabica ~284.55 (+3.85), high 288.30; Mar ~278.65, Dec/Mar inverse widening (ICE via TradingView)
Weaker Brazilian real encourages grower selling (Bloomberg)

cocoa.fundamental: The tile now follows Mar (~5,222, +38) after the roll; the small overnight bounce does not change the supply story. Rising ICE-certified cocoa stocks add to the ample-supply picture from steady Ivory Coast arrivals, and that outweighs early talk of dry weather hurting the mid-crop for now.
events: Mar cocoa ~5,222 (+38), Dec ~5,078 in early trade (ICE via TradingView)
Rising ICE cocoa inventories pressure prices (Barchart)
Dry West African weather keeps mid-crop questions open (ADMIS)
